factual_claims.claim: AS Tallink Grupp’s 2025 performance weakened year on year amid economic uncertainty, particularly in Finland, subdued consumer and business confidence, geopolitical tensions, inflation, higher taxes and reduced cargo demand.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The year 2025 proved to be challenging. Tallink’s results were particularly affected by economic uncertainty in our largest market, Finland. The overall unfavourable environment in the region has constrained private consumer confidence and adversely affected cargo flows... The Group’s operations remained under pressure from evolving consumer behaviour and adverse microeconomic trends in its core markets of Finland, Sweden, and Estonia. Consumer and business spending continued to be restrained, reflecting the combined impact of persistent inflation, elevated geopolitical tensions, and volatility of global trade conditions... In Estonia, the reduced VAT rate of accommodation services increased to 14% from 1 January 2025. Additionally, income tax for both individuals and business entities increased from 20% to 22% from 1 January 2025... The number of cargo units transported decreased by 19.2% to 245,004

candidate_sentences.text: The Board intends to propose a 2026 dividend of EUR 0.06 per share.

verified_key_information_units.information: FY2025 headline financial performance: revenue decreased to EUR 765.3M (from EUR 785.8M in FY2024), EBITDA declined to EUR 130.1M (from EUR 175.2M), net profit fell to EUR 17.3M or EUR 0.023 per share (from EUR 40.3M).

candidate_sentences.text: Revenue declined 2.6% to EUR 765.3 million from EUR 785.8 million.
EBITDA fell 25.7% to EUR 130.1 million from EUR 175.2 million, reducing the EBITDA margin from 22.3% to 17.0%.
Net profit fell 57.1% to EUR 17.3 million, or EUR 0.023 per share compared with EUR 0.054 in 2024.

verified_key_information_units.information: FY2025 transported volumes decreased: passengers to 5,531,132 (-0.9%), cargo units to 245,004 (-19.2%), passenger vehicles to 760,473 (-2.2%).

candidate_sentences.text: Passengers decreased 0.9% to 5.53 million, cargo units fell 19.2% to 245,004, and passenger vehicles declined 2.2% to 760,473.

verified_key_information_units.information: Performance driven by economic uncertainty in Finland impacting demand and lower depreciation from aligning vessel useful lives to 45 years.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Letter from CEO; Management Report factors

candidate_sentences.text: AS Tallink Grupp’s 2025 performance weakened year on year amid economic uncertainty, particularly in Finland, subdued consumer and business confidence, geopolitical tensions, inflation, higher taxes and reduced cargo demand.
Depreciation and amortisation decreased 18.4% to EUR 79.8 million, mainly because the estimated useful lives of most cruise and passenger vessels were aligned to 45 years and three vessels were sold.

verified_key_information_units.information: Segment performance: Estonia-Finland route revenue increased EUR 1.7M to EUR 314.5M but segment result fell EUR 10.9M; Finland-Sweden routes revenue decreased EUR 3.3M to EUR 225.5M with segment result down EUR 1.5M; Estonia-Sweden routes revenue down EUR 12.1M to EUR 85.3M but segment result improved to loss of EUR 1.2M.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Sales and Results by Segments section

candidate_sentences.text: Estonia–Finland passenger volumes increased 1.8%, but cargo volumes declined 20.0%; revenue rose to EUR 314.5 million while the segment result fell by EUR 10.9 million.
Finland–Sweden revenue decreased to EUR 225.5 million and its result fell to EUR 1.3 million, partly reflecting 68 days of maintenance for Silja Serenade and Baltic Princess.
Estonia–Sweden revenue declined to EUR 85.3 million, while its loss improved to EUR 1.2 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity position as at 31 Dec 2025: net debt EUR 432.4M (net debt/EBITDA 3.3), cash and cash equivalents EUR 13.5M, unused credit lines EUR 96.9M, total liquidity buffer EUR 110.4M.

candidate_sentences.text: Net debt remained broadly stable at EUR 432.4 million, while the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio was 3.3 versus 3.1 at year-end 2024.
Cash declined to EUR 13.5 million, partly because EUR 44.6 million of dividends and EUR 11.3 million of related income tax were paid.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital investments of EUR 33.0M in FY2025, mainly for maintenance and refurbishment of cruise ferries Baltic Princess and Silja Serenade, including technical upgrades, and IT systems improvement.

candidate_sentences.text: Capital expenditure increased to EUR 33.0 million from EUR 22.4 million, largely for vessel maintenance and refurbishment.

verified_key_information_units.information: Dividends paid EUR 44.6M (EUR 0.06 per share) in 2025; Management Board proposed dividend of EUR 0.06 per share for 2026.

candidate_sentences.text: Cash declined to EUR 13.5 million, partly because EUR 44.6 million of dividends and EUR 11.3 million of related income tax were paid.
The Board intends to propose a 2026 dividend of EUR 0.06 per share.

verified_key_information_units.information: Q4 2025 results: passenger volume 1.3M (-0.3% YoY), revenue EUR 188.0M (+2.4% YoY), EBITDA EUR 27.6M (+7.3% YoY), net profit EUR 12.2M (vs net loss EUR 5.2M in Q4 2024).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Results of Fourth Quarter section; Key Figures

candidate_sentences.text: Fourth-quarter results improved: revenue rose 2.4% to EUR 188.0 million, EBITDA increased to EUR 27.6 million, and net profit recovered to EUR 12.2 million from a EUR 5.2 million loss.

verified_key_information_units.information: Fleet status: 11 vessels operated at year-end (2 shuttle, 6 passenger, 3 chartered out); sale of three vessels optimizing cost base; three vessels chartered out with extended agreements; shuttle vessels transitioning to biomethane fuel.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report vessel details; Letter from CEO on biomethane; Events section

candidate_sentences.text: Depreciation and amortisation decreased 18.4% to EUR 79.8 million, mainly because the estimated useful lives of most cruise and passenger vessels were aligned to 45 years and three vessels were sold.
The Group sold Star I, Regal Star and Sailor, reduced vessels in lay-up to zero by the third quarter, and ended the year with three vessels chartered out.

details.completeness_justification: All key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, K6, K7, K8, and K9 are all PRESENT with supporting sentences identified. The summary captures the core material meaning of each criterion without needing inference. The overall picture of FY2025 performance, volume changes, drivers, segment results, liquidity, capital investments, dividends, Q4 results, and fleet status are all sufficiently covered.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. It consistently describes a decline in Tallink Grupp's 2025 performance across revenue, passengers, cargo, and profitability metrics, with logical explanations for changes (e.g., economic uncertainty, vessel sales, maintenance). All comparisons (year-on-year, segment-level) are clear and non-contradictory. The summary organizes information logically: overall performance trends are presented first, followed by detailed breakdowns of revenue, profitability, segments, capital expenditure, and cash flow. There is no unnecessary repetition, and all relationships (e.g., lower depreciation supporting net profit despite weaker operating performance) are logically consistent. The fourth-quarter improvement is presented as a contrast to the annual decline, which is coherent. No arithmetic contradictions are present or implied, as the summary does not claim exhaustive additivity of segment figures to consolidated totals.
